records.title: Feature exploration/request: nested data (nth-degree recursion)
Hierarchical Data Pattern | Lanvige's Zen Garden
records.body:
Hierarchical Data Pattern | Lanvige's Zen Garden

https://ift.tt/3dlbBFn

About 0 Minutes

Tree Structure 是一种很常见的需求（像分类，目录等），关系数据库中，有几种经典模式：

  • Adjacency List Model
  • Nested Set Model
  • Nested Interval Model
  • Materialized Path Model

关于这几种模式的一些通用介绍，参考：

  • http://www.dbazine.com/oracle/or-articles/tropashko4/
  • http://leopard.in.ua/2013/07/11/storing-trees-in-rdbms/
  • https://vadimtropashko.wordpress.com/2008/08/09/one-more-nested-intervals-vs-adjacency-list-comparison/
  • https://github.com/ynu/learn-mongodb/tree/master/src/data-model

Ruby Toolbox 中一些对 Tree 的通用库：

  • https://www.ruby-toolbox.com/categories/Active_Record_Nesting

1. Adjacency List Model

Use ancestry. It has more powerful query capabilities as it implements the materialized path pattern, as opposed to acts_as_tree that implements adjacency list.

父节点引用的方式（也称父节点引用模式），将树形结构中的每个节点单独存放到一个文档中，并在每个文档中保存节点的父节点引用。 考虑以下数据结构：

id type(*optional) parent_id depth
1 course 1
5 section 1 1
7 courseware 5 2
8 courseware 5 2

查询出该课程：

.1 优势

实现起来特别简单，因为只是存储 parent_id，没有多余的算法。

.2 不足

如果想构造一根树，在 DB 查询时，需要太多次循环调用。产生性能问题。

Recursive CTEs

Generating Depth based tree from Hierarchical Data in MySQL (no CTEs)

.3 Rails 实现

Organise ActiveRecord model into a tree structure

  • https://github.com/stefankroes/ancestry
  • https://github.com/take-five/acts_as_ordered_tree

records.title: Feedback about manual section "with-recursive-clause"
records.body:
While the suggested way to build recursive CTE is fine and works perfectly, it has the following flaw: it relies on dynamic DSL generation, what could lead to runtime errors in case of scheme changes. 
I'd like to suggest alternative approach, which is closer to actual SQL query building, when all fields are derived from the generated DSL. For example, the query from the docs:

```sql
CommonTableExpression<?> cte = name("t").fields(
  "id",
  "name",
  "path"
).as(
  select(
    DIRECTORY.ID,
    DIRECTORY.LABEL,
    DIRECTORY.LABEL)
  .from(DIRECTORY)
  .where(DIRECTORY.PARENT_ID.isNull())
  .unionAll(
  select(
    DIRECTORY.ID,
    DIRECTORY.LABEL,
    field(name("t", "path"), VARCHAR)
      .concat("\\")
      .concat(DIRECTORY.LABEL))
  .from(table(name("t")))
  .join(DIRECTORY)
  .on(field(name("t", "id"), INTEGER)
    .eq(DIRECTORY.PARENT_ID)))
);

System.out.println(
    create.withRecursive(cte)
          .selectFrom(cte)
          .fetch()
);

``` 

Could be rewritten like this:

```sql
var cteName = name("t");

var pathField = DIRECTORY.LABEL.as("path");
var guardClause = select(
    DIRECTORY.ID,
    DIRECTORY.LABEL,
    pathField)
    .from(DIRECTORY)
    .where(DIRECTORY.PARENT_ID.isNull());
var guardClauseTable = guardClause.asTable(cteName);

var recursiveClause = select(
    DIRECTORY.ID,
    DIRECTORY.LABEL,
    guardClauseTable.field(pathField)
        .concat("\\")
        .concat(DIRECTORY.LABEL))
    .from(table(guardClauseTable.getQualifiedName()))
    .join(DIRECTORY)
    .on(guardClauseTable.field(DIRECTORY.ID).eq(DIRECTORY.PARENT_ID));


var cte = cteName.as(guardClause.unionAll(recursiveClause));

System.out.println(dslContext.withRecursive(cte)
    .selectFrom(cte)
    .fetch());
```

One thing to note here: I had to use `table(guardClauseTable.getQualifiedName())` instead of simply `guardClauseTable`, because latter produces StackOverflowException

----
See: https://www.jooq.org/doc/latest/manual/sql-building/sql-statements/with-recursive-clause/

records.title: refactor(locations): migrate from tag-based storage to dedicated locations table
records.body:
## Background

Locations are currently stored as tags with `tag_type ∈ {country, city, address}` (introduced in #184). This works for the CRUD MVP but will not scale to location-based queries.

## Problem

When we add "assign location to item" and need queries like _"find all items in Kraków or any address in Kraków"_, the tag-based approach requires a recursive walk up the tag hierarchy:

```sql
-- current approach — fragile and slow on large datasets
SELECT DISTINCT i.* FROM items i
JOIN item_tags it ON it.item_id = i.id
JOIN tags t ON t.id = it.tag_id
WHERE t.id = :city_id
   OR t.parent_tag_id = :city_id
   OR t.parent_tag_id IN (SELECT id FROM tags WHERE parent_tag_id = :city_id)
```

## Proposed schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE locations (
    id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name      TEXT NOT NULL,
    address   TEXT,
    type      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(type IN ('country', 'city', 'address')),
    parent_id TEXT REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_locations_user ON locations(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_locations_parent ON locations(parent_id);

CREATE TABLE item_locations (
    item_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    location_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, location_id)
);
```

With a recursive CTE, the subtree query becomes clean and indexable:

```sql
WITH subtree AS (
    SELECT id FROM locations WHERE id = :root_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT l.id FROM locations l JOIN subtree s ON l.parent_id = s.id
)
SELECT DISTINCT i.* FROM items i
JOIN item_locations il ON il.item_id = i.id
WHERE il.location_id IN (SELECT id FROM subtree);
```

## Migration plan

1. Add `locations` and `item_locations` tables (new migration)
2. Migrate existing location tags → `locations` rows (one-time data migration in the same migration file)
3. Remove location tag types from the tag system
4. Update domain, server fns, and MCP tools to use the new table
5. Update `/locations` CRUD page to call new server functions

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `locations` and `item_locations` tables exist with proper FK constraints and indexes
- [ ] Existing location data migrated from tags
- [ ] Location CRUD page works as before
- [ ] Item detail page allows assigning one or more locations
- [ ] Query "items in location X (including descendants)" returns correct results

Shortest-Cycle-Containing-Target-Node
records.body:
You are given a two-dimensional list of integers graph representing a directed graph as an adjacency list. You are also given an integer target.

Return the length of a shortest cycle that contains target. If a solution does not exist, return -1.

Constraints

n, m ≤ 250 where n and m are the number of rows and columns in graph
